+# ADR 0001: Increase Pricing Cache TTL to 3600 Seconds
+
+## Status
+Accepted
+
+## Context
+
+The pricing service currently uses a Prompt Cache TTL (time-to-live) of 900 seconds (15 minutes). This relatively short cache window results in frequent cache evictions and regeneration, particularly for workloads with consistent pricing queries throughout a business day. As users interact with pricing features, the cache frequently expires, forcing the system to recompute cached responses and incurring additional computational overhead. The Anthropic Prompt Cache infrastructure supports cache retention for up to one hour within a single session, allowing for more aggressive caching strategies without architectural compromise.
+
+Increasing the cache TTL would reduce the frequency of cache misses, improve response latency for repeated queries, and lower overall computational cost by retaining cached responses longer. This change aligns with observed usage patterns where pricing queries are often repeated within the same user session or across users accessing similar product features.
+
+## Decision
+
+We will increase the pricing cache TTL from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds (1 hour). This change maximizes the benefit of Prompt Cache within its supported session window while maintaining reasonable freshness guarantees for pricing data. The 3600-second window provides a practical middle ground: it accommodates typical user sessions without requiring cache invalidation logic or introducing stale pricing concerns in normal operational scenarios.
+
+This change is implemented as a configuration update to the cache TTL parameter in the pricing service initialization code. No architectural changes or additional infrastructure are required.
+
+## Consequences
+
+With this change, pricing queries within the same session will experience higher cache hit rates, resulting in faster response times and reduced API request volumes. The broader cache window means users will see more consistent pricing data within their session duration, which aligns with user expectations that prices do not fluctuate within a single interaction.
+
+However, pricing updates or corrections that occur during a 3600-second window will not be reflected until the cache expires or the user starts a new session. This trade-off is acceptable given that pricing data typically changes infrequently during operational hours and users can request an explicit refresh if needed. Teams should be aware that cache invalidation during pricing emergencies will require either waiting for natural expiration or implementing explicit cache-clear mechanisms.
